Course catalogue

Courses and lesson supplements

Every walkable lesson, grouped into a course for its trade and a course for its strand, in ladder order. Each lesson has a supplement: a glossary, key concepts, safety notes quoted from the room records, self-check questions and a worksheet. Nothing here certifies anybody; lessons are unverified general practice.

Glossary terms
2486
  • No course certifies, qualifies or permits anybody. Lessons are unverified general practice.
  • Prerequisites are advice about order. Nothing is locked.
  • K-12 bands are read from the schools offer by a stated rule. They are not a placement.
  • Seat time is counted, not timed: no scenario declares minutes.
  • AUTHORED and DERIVED: every course is a grouping and an order chosen by the rules printed under `rules`; every name, title, room label and count is READ from the registry that owns it. Nothing is fetched and no model runs.
  • unverified general practice. The lessons a course lists have not been reviewed by a journey-level practitioner, and grouping them does not change that.
  • no course certifies, qualifies or permits anybody to do anything. Finishing every lesson in a course leaves a learner with exactly the standing they started with.
  • prerequisites are the ladder's advice about order. Nothing is locked, and the unaided verification gate that schools/ declares stays where it is.
  • K-12 bands are DERIVED from the words of each band's offer in schools/; they are a reading of that offer, not a placement by any teacher or district. School districts named elsewhere remain PROPOSED partners.
  • no minutes are given: no scenario declares a duration, so a course counts seat runs instead of inventing a time.

World training modules

Practice sets composed by a stated rule from the worlds' own registries: worksites by district, walkable Bay restoration sites, the wilds work sites and the robot yard. Each step is an existing step kind and names a real registry id.

AUTHORED by rule. Unverified general practice: nothing here certifies anybody, and no duration or credential is stated.

Structural worksites Worksites by district 30

📝 Greeted by: Entry supervisor — The entry is authorised for conditions, not for people. Ask me which conditions. agents/registry/crews.json#crews.confined-space-crew.roles.entry-supervisor.greeting

Omega Hive: SCRIPTED, no AI model, the device's speech synthesis, on a click, AUTHORED personalities.

Brief, quoted from the registry

  • Put one welder inside a tank to run a seam, with the space isolated and tested first, an attendant who never goes in, and a count out by name. worksites/registry/worksites.json#sites[1].job
  • Carry a load the cab cannot see land, high over the stacks, on one signaller's hands and one rigger's weight. worksites/registry/worksites.json#sites[2].job
  • Pick one steel member off the supply pad and set it in the ring with the plan read out loud first, one signaller, and nobody under the load. worksites/registry/worksites.json#sites[6].job
  • Run one deck seam under a hot-work permit that names this bay only, with a fire watch posted where the sparks land and held through the post-work period. worksites/registry/worksites.json#sites[7].job

Steps, in order

  1. crew entry-supervisor: "What are you authorising?"
  2. crew attendant: "What counts as contact?"
  3. walkaround Fume extraction: running and pulling at the work, not past your face
  4. crew attendant: "Why do you never go in?"
  5. crew entry-supervisor: "Why isolate before testing?"
  6. simulator Weld Bead Run · Tank shell seam

  9. station Rigging & Material Handling
  10. simulator Load Chart Judgment · Terminal heavy list
  11. walkaround Radio and whistle: checked both ways on a working channel before the first pick, and the channel is one nobody else on the site is on
  12. simulator Rigging Signal Call · Blind terminal pick
  13. simulator Tower Crane Lift · Oakland terminal lift
  14. crew signalperson: "Can two of you signal at once?"
  15. crew rigger: "Why this hitch and not another?"
  16. crew lift-director: "What if the lift changes?"
  17. crew lift-director: "What is in a lift plan?"
  18. simulator Load Chart Judgment · Yard pick list
  19. walkaround Line of sight: the operator can read your hands from every planned position
  20. simulator Rigging Signal Call · First lift card
  21. simulator Tower Crane Lift · Bay high-steel lift
  22. walkaround The load path: walked end to end, nothing and nobody under it
  23. crew rigger: "How do you know what it weighs?"
  24. crew lift-director: "What if the lift changes?"
  25. crew permit-holder: "What does a hot work permit cover?"
  26. walkaround Welding screens: standing and closed - nobody flashes off your arc
  27. walkaround Fire watch kit: extinguisher charged and in reach, combustibles cleared

  29. crew fire-watch: "How long do you stay after?"

Earthworks & Plant worksites Worksites by district 21

📡 Greeted by: Utility locator — Paint on the ground is a guess with a tolerance. Ask me how big the tolerance is. agents/registry/crews.json#crews.trench-crew.roles.locator.greeting

Omega Hive: SCRIPTED, no AI model, the device's speech synthesis, on a click, AUTHORED personalities.

Brief, quoted from the registry

  • Cut a shallow drainage run through the upland fill above the tide line, cell by cell, with the ground inspected before the first bite and after anything that changes it. worksites/registry/worksites.json#sites[0].job
  • Open one trench cell along the levee toe with the buried services marked and proved first, a spotter in the operator's eyeline, and the cut held shallow where the marks run. worksites/registry/worksites.json#sites[3].job
  • Build one scaffold bay in stage order from bedded sills to guardrails, hold the drop zone, and hand it to a competent person to inspect and tag before anyone stands on it. worksites/registry/worksites.json#sites[5].job

Steps, in order

  1. crew locator: "How good are the marks?"
  2. walkaround The trench edge: spoil set back, no load surcharging the cut
  3. walkaround Bucket teeth and pins: teeth tight, pins keepered, no cracks at the ears
  4. crew spotter: "What is your one call?"
  5. simulator Excavator Trench Cut · Seismic retrofit cut
  6. crew trench-competent-person: "How often does it get inspected?"
  7. crew locator: "What does proving a mark mean?"
  8. crew locator: "How good are the marks?"
  9. crew trench-competent-person: "What are you reading the ground for?"
  10. walkaround Tracks and rollers: tension right, no cut pads or leaking rollers
  11. crew spotter: "Where do you stand?"
  12. simulator Excavator Trench Cut · Old-fill utility cut
  13. walkaround The trench edge: spoil set back, no load surcharging the cut
  14. crew locator: "What does proving a mark mean?"
  15. walkaround Sills and bearing: full bearing on grade, no blocks or debris packing
  16. walkaround Frames plumb and level: plumb both ways, level across the bay
  17. crew ground-tender: "Why not just send everything up at once?"
  18. simulator Scaffold Bay Build · Yard training bay
  19. walkaround Brace pins: every brace pinned home, none sprung
  20. station Scaffold & Fall Protection
  21. crew ground-tender: "What is a drop zone?"

Brief, quoted from the registry

  • Drive the rover over AUTHORED litter items (types read from ambient/) to collect them all. robotics/registry/robotics.json#envs["world.litter-pickup"].brief
  • turn toward the nearest open target (proportional on bearing) robotics/registry/robotics.json#envs["world.litter-pickup"].reference_policy.steps[0]
  • drive at a speed that falls with the heading error robotics/registry/robotics.json#envs["world.litter-pickup"].reference_policy.steps[1]
  • veer away when an obstacle sits within 2 m ahead robotics/registry/robotics.json#envs["world.litter-pickup"].reference_policy.steps[2]

Steps, in order

  1. rover watch: the rover yard replays the reference steps on a seeded loop and stores nothing
  2. rover drive: the same env at the keys in the Robotics lab, recorded by the lab as its existing world-teleop episode

How the catalogue is put together

  • trade_course one per hall of pack/registry/halls.json: the lessons standing in that hall, grouped under the hall's district
  • strand_course one per room of web/interiors.py: every lesson whose strand it is, across halls
  • order ladder depth (lessons.json#ladder.depth), then the lessons registry order
  • prerequisites the ladder's own edges, split into those inside the course and those pointing at another course; advice about order, never a gate
  • seat_time counts only - seats bound to the course halls, seat runs, walkaround points and crew asks; no minutes, because no scenario declares a duration
  • bands · K-5 · rests_on no machine seats and no station quizzes
  • bands · K-5 · max_tier fundamentals
  • bands · K-5 · kinds walk, placard, advisor
  • bands · K-5 · why awareness only: a K-5 lesson is one walked through rooms, read at the door and asked of an advisor - no seat, no walkaround of a seat, no crew, no station, no crib check
  • bands · 6-8 · rests_on home modules at fundamentals tier plus class station work
  • bands · 6-8 · max_tier fundamentals
  • bands · 6-8 · kinds walk, placard, advisor, station, crib
  • bands · 6-8 · why fundamentals tier and class-stage steps only: no simulator floor time is offered to this band
  • bands · 9-10 · rests_on simulator floor time
  • bands · 9-10 · max_tier applied
  • bands · 9-10 · kinds walk, placard, advisor, station, crib, walkaround, sim, crew
  • bands · 9-10 · why up to applied tier, class and floor steps
  • bands · 11-12 · rests_on mastery-tier modules
  • bands · 11-12 · max_tier mastery
  • bands · 11-12 · kinds walk, placard, advisor, station, crib, walkaround, sim, crew
  • bands · 11-12 · why every tier, class and floor steps
  • supplement · glossary the rooms and off-room places the lesson stands in (meaning: web/interiors.py purpose, lessons.json off_room_places), every tool of the hall's district crib (meaning: the tool's own `use` line), every PPE item and hazard on the condition record of a room the lesson walks (meaning: where it is listed - the record gives no definition, so none is written), the seats, scenarios and walkaround points the lesson runs (meaning: task, brief, check), the advisors and crew roles it asks (meaning: role, job)
  • supplement · concepts the lesson's own `why`, every step note, then from the owning registry: a station's lesson and doctrine, an advisor or crew topic's `say` (or, for a `read` topic, the binding it is read from), a crew role's stop condition, a scenario's `teaches`, a walkaround point's check, and the crib drill contract
  • supplement · safety labelled unverified general practice. The condition record of every room the lesson walks, quoted in the exact form the 3D page's condLine() prints it (a placard hangs only where the record asks for PPE), the walkaround fault line and the crew stop-work lines of the steps that bind them, the checklist of a station step, and the lesson's limits
  • supplement · questions one per walk, placard, advisor, walkaround, sim, crew and station step, plus one crib drill item for every lesson (two when the lesson runs the crib check); each answer is a registry id with the pointer it resolves at, the distractors are siblings from the same record, and the correct option's position is index arithmetic
  • supplement · worksheet one line per step: the step's own `do` line, verbatim, and a fill-in prompt for its kind
  • supplement · where the rooms and places walked, the hall's district crib, the advisors asked (and the room each stands in), the seats and scenarios run, the crews asked, the stations taken, and links to the lesson, the hall in 3D and the ladder
